def is_possible(first_day, second_day):
    days = ["monday", "tuesday", "wednesday", "thursday", "friday", "saturday", "sunday"]
    index_first = days.index(first_day)
    index_second = days.index(second_day)
    
    # Calculate the difference in days between the first and second day of the week
    diff = (index_second - index_first + 7) % 7
    
    # Check if the difference is 1 (i.e., the first day comes immediately before the second day)
    return diff == 1

def check_months(first_day_name, second_day_name):
    weekdays = ["monday", "tuesday", "wednesday", "thursday", "friday", "saturday", "sunday"]
    first_day_index = weekdays.index(first_day_name)
    second_day_index = weekdays.index(second_day_name)
    
    for year in range(1900, 2100):  # Check for years between 1900 and 2099
        current_month_start = date(year, 1, 1)
        if current_month_start.weekday() == first_day_index:
            next_month_start = current_month_start.replace(day=28) + timedelta(days=4)  # Move to the next month
            if next_month_start.month != current_month_start.month and next_month_start.weekday() == second_day_index:
                return "YES"
    return "NO"

import sys
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

def check_months(day1, day2):
    # Mapping of day names to their indices (Monday=0, ..., Sunday=6)
    days_of_week = ["monday", "tuesday", "wednesday", "thursday", "friday", "saturday", "sunday"]
    index1 = days_of_week.index(day1)
    index2 = days_of_week.index(day2)
    
    # Function to get the first day of the next month
    def first_day_next_month(year, month):
        return datetime(year, month + 1, 1).weekday()
    
    # Check all non-leap years
    for year in range(1900, 2101):  # Arbitrary large range to cover possible years
        for month in range(1, 13):
            if first_day_next_month(year, month) == index2:
                current_day = first_day_next_month(year, month - 1)
                if current_day == index1:
                    return "YES"
    return "NO"
